item.title: Anthropic plans IPO event with JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon
item.description: Anthropic PBC is preparing for a live-streamed event featuring CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon. This event is aimed at marketing their upcoming initial public offering, which might break records. The IPO is set to begin marketing shortly and is planned to debut before the Thanksgiving holiday. Anthropic is targeting an offering size similar to SpaceX's IPO, which raised significant funding.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Anthropic PBC is planning a live-streamed event, at which co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei will discuss the Claude chatbot maker’s initial public offering with JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon, according to a person familiar with the matter.The meeting is part of the marketing effort for Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking IPO. The offering is expected to formally begin marketing as soon as early Tuesday ahead of pricing and the Nasdaq debut of its shares before the US Thanksgiving holiday, Bloomberg has reported.The Amodei-Dimon chat is expected to be held around lunchtime Friday in New York, a similar to but less extravagant event than the one conducted with Elon Musk in June as part of SpaceX’s $86.2 billion listing, said the person, who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.Representatives for Anthropic and JPMorgan declined to comment.JPMorgan, one of the 22 banks working on the deal, is leading domestic retail marketing and share allocations for Anthropic’s IPO. The company has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the listing overall, people familiar with the matter have said.Anthropic is targeting an offering as big as SpaceX’s in its record-setting debut, or bigger, Bloomberg News reported. SpaceX’s IPO in June raised $86.2 billion including overallotment shares. Potential investors were discussing valuations in the range of $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion for the company, people familiar with the matter have said, after the US midterm elections last week forced a rethink of artificial intelligence valuations.Separately, JPMorgan has embraced Anthropic’s Claude Code product across the bank beyond software engineers, according to an article on Anthropic’s website posted on Monday.Citigroup is coordinating the international retail offering, Bloomberg has reported, encompassing offerings in the UK and parts of Europe, Canada, Japan and Australia.Goldman Sachs has the coveted lead-left role on the IPO, while Morgan Stanley is acting as stabilization agent, according to Anthropic’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

item.title: Japan's Nikkei surges nearly 3% as AI stks extend rebound
item.description: Japan's Nikkei index jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday as AI and semiconductor stocks recovered from Friday's sharp selloff. SoftBank Group surged over 14%, leading the tech-driven rally alongside chip equipment makers, despite overnight losses in Nvidia shares and cautious sentiment near key resistance levels.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Nagar
item.content:encoded: Japan's Nikkei share average climbed nearly 3% on Tuesday, extending its recovery from a sharp technology-led selloff last week as artificial intelligence-related stocks staged a strong rebound, Reuters reported.The Nikkei rose 2.88% to 60,471.05 by 0158 GMT, recovering most of the losses suffered during Friday's steep decline over the past two trading sessions. The broader Topix index advanced 2.27% to 3,904.67.The rebound followed a nearly 6% slump in the Nikkei on Friday, when AI-related stocks came under heavy selling pressure amid concerns that the US Congress could slow investment in artificial intelligence following the Democrats' decisive victory in the midterm elections.Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks rally after US tech surge, oil slumpAccording to Reuters, the latest gains were driven by renewed buying in technology and semiconductor stocks, although investors remained cautious about the possibility of the Nikkei crossing the 61,000 mark.Technology investor SoftBank Group surged 14.38% on Tuesday, while semiconductor equipment makers Advantest and Tokyo Electron gained 4.93% and 5.66%, respectively. Memory-chip maker Kioxia jumped 7.6%.The gains came despite Nvidia shares falling 4.2% overnight amid controversy surrounding its CEO Jensen Huang. However, investors appeared to view the developments as largely company-specific rather than a broader threat to the artificial intelligence industry, Reuters reported.Read more: US stocks: Dow rockets 1,100 points, S&P over 2% as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumpsKioxia's rally also came as some investors unwound leveraged positions following Friday's selloff to avoid margin calls. Outstanding margin-buying positions in the stock declined to 48.22 million shares from 52.85 million a day earlier, according to Tokyo Stock Exchange data.Kioxia accounts for a significant portion of outstanding margin-buying positions after emerging as a major contributor to the Nikkei's rally to a record high in June. The stock has subsequently faced pressure amid deteriorating sentiment towards AI-related shares.Elsewhere, JX Advanced Metals rose 2.2% after the semiconductor materials maker raised its net profit forecast for the financial year ending next March by 14%.However, gains across the broader market were not uniform. Toyota Motor fell 1.63%, making it the biggest drag on the Topix, while soy sauce maker Kikkoman plunged 13% to become the biggest percentage loser on the Nikkei.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
